主要内容: Payless ShoeSource has filed for bankruptcy protection, marking a significant downturn for the U.S. shoe retailer. The company has already begun closing its 2,500 U.S. stores, with plans to keep all stores open until at least the end of March and the majority until May. The filing, made on Monday night, follows the start of liquidation sales for its U.S. stores. Payless has approximately $470 million in outstanding debt, and its previous bankruptcy filing in April 2017 eliminated nearly 700 stores and $435 million in debt. The company faces challenges from larger competitors like TJX Companies and DSW, and its recent losses in 2018 and 2017 highlight its financial struggles. Payless also blamed its initial bankruptcy filing on outdated inventory management and port strikes that delayed shipments before the Easter holidays. The company aims to leverage its strong brand name and growth in Latin America, but unanticipated supplier delays have forced it to sell inventory at deep-discount prices. With limited cash, Payless was unable to fully implement its omnichannel strategy, rolling out unified shopping capabilities to only 200 stores.
